writing.text:
Excited to share a new local-AI benchmarking project built around the Intel Arc Pro B65.

Our goal is simple: measure what modern AI workloads can do on a single workstation GPU, without sending data to the cloud. We’ll track inference speed, memory efficiency, model size, and real-world usability across popular open-source models.

This is especially relevant for teams exploring privacy-first AI, edge deployment, and cost-effective local inference. The Arc Pro B65 brings serious compute to the table, and we want to see how it performs under realistic conditions.

Stay tuned for benchmarks, methodology, and practical takeaways. If you’re working with local AI, I’d love to hear what matters most to you. Let's build better local AI together.

#LocalAI #IntelArc #AI

SEO optimizes content to rank in traditional search results, driving clicks to your site. AEO optimizes for answer engines—AI assistants, chatbots, and featured snippets—so your brand is cited directly in the answer.

SEO targets keywords, backlinks, and page experience. AEO targets clarity, entity clarity, structured data, and source credibility.

In practice, SEO still matters because AI engines often draw from indexed, authoritative pages. But AEO shifts focus from “get clicked” to “get cited.” For marketers, that means creating concise, factual, well-structured content that answers questions directly and is easy for machines to verify.

- **Privacy and control:** Running AI locally keeps data and prompts on your own hardware, reducing reliance on third-party cloud services.
- **Cost and access:** After the initial GPU investment, local inference can be cheaper and avoids API rate limits, usage fees, or service outages.
- **Customization and experimentation:** You can fine-tune, modify, or test models freely without depending on external providers or their restrictions.
